subject: OrderForm: capacity add & implementation concurrency (DataSync)
messages:
From: Maya Shah <procure@datasync.com>
To: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: DataSync Legal <legal@datasync.com>; Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Add capacity & implementation concurrency for Q3 rollout

Hi Chloe,

Following our internal planning, we need to request a formal change order to add 120k token-throughput units (phased across Jul-Sep) and to allow parallel implementation streams for two product lines (payments + search). Procurement asked me to capture the ask now so we can align legal and finance. Key asks: 

- Add 120k tokens across Q3 (30k Jul, 40k Aug, 50k Sep)
- Update SOW Exhibit A to split implementation milestones into Stream A (payments) and Stream B (search) and allow concurrency during overlapping weeks 4–8
- Confirm any uplift to monthly fees and whether a pro-rated invoice will be issued for July

Can you confirm next steps and an estimated timeline for a redline/Order Form supplement? We have a hard go/no-go by 2026-06-30 for budgeting.

Thanks,
Maya Shah
Sr. Procurement Manager
DataSync Corp
[Attachment: capacity_request_summary.pdf (pdf, 22KB)]

Subject: Re: Request: Add capacity & implementation concurrency for Q3 rollout

Maya — thanks for the clear breakdown. We can do this; next steps I propose: 

1) I’ll draft an Order Form supplement + SOW exhibit that splits the milestones and includes the phased capacity add.
2) Laura (legal) will do a high-level pass on the redline for any MSA conflicts.
3) We’ll return a tracked redline and an implementation matrix with expected cutover windows — target EOD Tue (tomorrow).

Two quick clarifications for scoping and pricing: 
- Do both product lines require dedicated reserved pools or can that capacity be shared with routing rules?
- Is DataSync expecting a single invoice with pro-rate, or separate invoices per product line?

I attached a first-pass supplement (docx) and a draft implementation matrix. If you prefer a call, I have openings 2–4pm PT today.

Cheers,
Chloe Martin

Redwood Inference

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: Add capacity & implementation concurrency for Q3 rollout

Chloe — I reviewed the supplement quickly. A few legal flags to tidy before external circulation: 

1) Concurrent implementation: add explicit language on acceptance criteria for each stream and a clause that prevents simultaneous failover obligations (we need to limit overlapping rollback liability).
2) Pricing uplift: define the monthly baseline and the method for proration — prefer simple pro-rate on days-of-service rather than token-weighted calculations.
3) Termination/rollback: for parallel streams, ask product to confirm rollback plan and any additional support SLAs (on-call windows).

I’ll insert inline comments in redline_orderform_v2.docx and put a short memo at the top of the SOW. If you want me to escalate to Commercial for a priced exception, let me know.

- Laura
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Add capacity & implementation concurrency for Q3 rollout

Quick notes from product/ops: 
- Capacity model: both streams can share a routed pool; we do not need dedicated reserved pools unless the customer requires strict isolation. Recommend shared pool with routing rules and a burst buffer for peak days.
- Rollback: we will build a sequencing plan to ensure Stream A has a prioritized KV cache warmup to limit latency spikes on Stream B. Requires one on-call engineer for first two weeks post-cutover.

I’ll add an operations appendix to the implementation_matrix outlining the cutover playbook and expected on-call coverage.

— Karthik
Director, Product
Redwood Inference

From: DataSync Legal <legal@datasync.com>

Cc: Maya Shah <procure@datasync.com>, Maria Santos <maria.santos@lawfirm.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: Add capacity & implementation concurrency for Q3 rollout

Chloe, Laura — thanks for the quick turnaround. We reviewed your redline and have three external asks:

1) Clarify SLA credits if concurrent streams cause a regional outage — DataSync needs a clear remediation ladder.
2) Add a 60-day notice for any fee increases tied to the phased capacity schedule (we want predictability).
3) Can Redwood accept a short carve that delays the invoice date for July until the July 15th payroll cut? That helps our cashflow.

Attached are our markups (pdf) and our counsel Maria has suggested alternative language for Section 4.3. Please confirm if proration per day is acceptable and whether Redwood can commit a named on-call engineer for the first 10 business days.

— DataSync Legal
[Attachment: datasync_markups.pdf (pdf, 34KB)]

- Laura will update the redline with explicit concurrent-stream acceptance criteria and SLA remediation ladder (we can accept the remediation ladder with a cap tied to monthly fees).
- We can confirm day-based proration and will accommodate the July invoice delay to Jul 15 for this order (finance to approve final schedule).
- Karthik will commit an on-call rotation for 10 business days; Jordan will confirm the named engineer Monday AM.

Would DataSync like a short 30-minute sync with Laura and Karthik tomorrow to close the legal language and operations appendix? If yes, I’ll send a calendar invite and a final doc version to sign via DocuSign.
